violated_contract: A credential revocation endpoint must not answer success unless the credential was actually removed. The mobile app renders any 2xx from DELETE /v1/apps/{app_id}/keys/{key_id} as a confirmed revocation (AddAppProvider.deleteApiKey awaits deleteApiKeyServer, which throws only on a non-200, and ApiKeysWidget then shows 'API key revoked successfully'), so a delete that matched no stored key while the route dropped the data layer's result left the user believing a credential was dead when nothing had been revoked.
canonical_prevention: Keep the deletion outcome from the data layer and classify a no-op revocation once at the route boundary as a refusal (404 'API key not found') instead of returning the generic success payload, so every client that treats 2xx as a confirmed mutation inherits the same classification rather than each caller deciding whether the delete happened.
